source.title: WRC Digest - A Summary of 2022
source.content:
Dear WCA Community,

2022 has been a productive year for the WCA Regulations Committee, and now the WRC would like to share with you some insight on the work we have done in the recent year. 

Firstly, 8 new members joined [our committee](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/teams-committees#WRC). So far, their contributions have been extremely welcome for the WRC, and we look forward to seeing what the future holds for our committee.

In the second half of 2022, the WRC concluded an investigation regarding competitions in Vietnam. For more details, see [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/posts/wrc-investigation-vietnamese-competitions-results-removal) announcement and [this](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1E-J8WRfld6mpbHslM3rW10fNSsXgkl2y/view?usp=share_link) investigation report.

Along with this investigation, we resolved many incidents, which you can find in the [Incidents log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents), here are the most noticeable ones:

1. During the inspection of a Megaminx attempt, the competitor caused an unintentional misalignment to the puzzle, possibly against [Regulation A3c1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A3c1). After careful review of the video footage, the WRC has decided not to DNF the attempt. None of the frames analyzed point to the face having moved beyond the allowed 36º (see [Regulation 10f2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#10f2)). See [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/63) incident log. Misalignments during inspection have been clarified with the February 2023 Regulations update.
2. A competitor used a Clock with a sticker (logo) placed on the side. The puzzle was determined to be competition-legal as there were no regulations  explicitly forbidding logos for Clock puzzles and the competitor is not likely to have gained an advantage. See [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/66) incident log. Clock hardware has been clarified with the February 2023 Regulations update.
3. A competitor claimed to be distracted after finishing the solve (i.e. stopping the timer), but before finishing the attempt (i.e. signing the score sheet), and requested an extra attempt. The WRC further discussed this incident and agreed that the original attempt should stay. For more details, see [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/69) incident log. [Regulation 11e](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#11e) and its guidelines have been clarified with the February 2023 Regulations update to not cause any further confusion.
4. After a competitor finished their solve, the timer was reset by either the judge or by the timer itself before the result was fully recorded on the score sheet. The video evidence showed the display but not the timer. Since the display was clearly shown in the evidence and it was working fine through the solve, WRC agreed that the original result shown on the display may stand. For more details, see [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/72) incident log.
5. A judge forgot to hold a sight blocker for a significant amount of time in a 3BLD attempt. The decision from the WRC was to keep the extra attempt. However, in the latter, the decision was overturned by the WCA Board of Directors, thus keeping the original attempt. For more details, see [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/78) incident log. The Regulations on sight blockers have been clarified in the February 2023 Regulations update. 

To conclude the digest, we would like to remind everyone about the importance of adhering to the WCA Regulations, Guidelines, and Policies. It is important to make sure you understand them properly to ensure they are followed during your official attempts.

If you have any WCA Regulations related questions, do not hesitate to contact us at [regulations@worldcubeassociation.org](mailto:regulations@worldcubeassociation.org), or to ask your questions in the [WCA Regulations](https://forum.worldcubeassociation.org/c/regulations/5) category on the WCA Forum.

translation.title: WCA 规则委员会工作简报：2022 年回顾
translation.content:
各位 WCA 社区成员：

2022 年，WCA 规则委员会完成了不少工作。我们希望通过这份简报，向大家介绍过去一年的工作情况。

首先，8 名新成员加入了[委员会](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/teams-committees#WRC)。他们的贡献给 WRC 带来了很大帮助，我们也期待委员会今后的发展。

2022 年下半年，WRC 完成了对越南比赛的调查。详情可参见[这篇公告](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/posts/wrc-investigation-vietnamese-competitions-results-removal)和[调查报告](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1E-J8WRfld6mpbHslM3rW10fNSsXgkl2y/view?usp=share_link)。

除这项调查外，我们还处理了许多意外事件，可在[意外事件日志](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents)中查看。以下是几起较值得关注的事件：

1. 一次五魔尝试的观察阶段，选手无意间使魔方发生了错层，可能违反[规则 A3c1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A3c1)。仔细审查视频后，WRC 决定不将该次尝试判为 DNF。所分析的视频画面均未显示该层转动超过允许的 36°（参见[规则 10f2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#10f2)）。事件记录见[这里](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/63)。2023 年 2 月的规则更新已进一步说明观察期间的错层问题。
2. 一名选手使用的魔表侧面贴有标志贴纸。由于当时没有规则明确禁止魔表上的标志，且选手不太可能因此获得优势，该魔表被认定可以用于比赛。事件记录见[这里](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/66)。2023 年 2 月的规则更新已进一步说明魔表的器材要求。
3. 一名选手在还原结束（即停止计时器）后、该次尝试结束（即在成绩单上签名）前，表示自己受到了干扰，并要求补赛。WRC 进一步讨论后，同意保留原尝试成绩。详情见[事件记录](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/69)。2023 年 2 月的规则更新已进一步说明[规则 11e](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#11e)及其指南，避免继续产生歧义。
4. 一名选手完成还原后，在成绩尚未完整记入成绩单前，计时器被裁判重置或自行重置。视频证据拍到了显示器，但没有拍到计时器。由于视频清楚显示了显示器，且它在整个还原过程中工作正常，WRC 同意保留显示器上显示的原成绩。详情见[事件记录](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/72)。
5. 一次三盲尝试中，裁判有相当长一段时间忘记放置遮挡物。WRC 决定保留补赛成绩，但之后 WCA 董事会推翻了这一决定，改为保留原尝试成绩。详情见[事件记录](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/78)。2023 年 2 月的规则更新已进一步说明遮挡物的相关规定。

最后，我们想提醒大家，遵守 WCA 规则、指南和政策非常重要。请确保自己正确理解这些规定，并在正式尝试中遵守。

如有 WCA 规则相关问题，欢迎通过 [regulations@worldcubeassociation.org](mailto:regulations@worldcubeassociation.org) 联系我们，也可以在 WCA 论坛的 [WCA 规则](https://forum.worldcubeassociation.org/c/regulations/5)板块提问。
